processes.name: Deal ticket extension and missing deal requests to Daren Farmer
processes.description: Schedulers and logistics staff email Daren Farmer to extend, roll or create Sitara deal tickets so that flow or allocated volumes on a meter are covered. Each request names the meter, the deal number and the dates or volumes, and Daren replies 'Done' or creates the deal by hand.
processes.stall_points: Every request depends on one person (Daren) to key the change, and requesters resend or chase ('one more time', 'I can't remember if I'd already sent you this'). Protected deal tickets block self-service corrections.
processes.automation: A request form or ticket queue that validates meter, deal and dates and applies simple extensions or rolls for approval. Flow-without-deal exceptions could be flagged automatically from allocation data.

processes.name: Nomination changes and revised nominations needing approval
processes.description: Counterparty nomination changes and revisions arrive by email or phone and are forwarded to Daren Farmer for approval before schedulers update Unify, Sitara or POPS. Schedulers also query odd nominations on meters.
processes.stall_points: Pipeline will not confirm the requested volume, so the nomination is revised and approval is requested by email ('Please advise'). Each change is forwarded and re-keyed by hand.
processes.automation: Parse counterparty nomination emails into a structured change record with the old and new volume, and route it for one-click approval. Push approved changes into the scheduling system.

processes.name: Pipeline cut and weekend activity reporting
processes.description: Schedulers email Daren and the group with gas cuts by pipelines such as El Paso and Oasis, and with weekend activity logs listing calls, cuts and balancing choices by meter. The cuts are entered in MOPS as estimates and the recipients are asked to check meters.
processes.stall_points: Cuts are relayed by email after the fact and the weekend log is resent as a revision, so recipients must reread it. Cuts are keyed into MOPS manually as estimates.
processes.automation: Capture cuts from pipeline notices into a shared structured log, auto-update the estimates in the scheduling system, and send one digest. A cut template would stop repeated revisions.

processes.name: Monthly Activity and Hours survey collection (Operations Pricing Model)
processes.description: Each month a survey is sent to all operations staff for completion and return to Shari Mao, with stat requests to individuals. Supervisors then chase the many late responders.
processes.stall_points: Few people respond by the deadline, which leads to reminder emails and a new deadline. People complain the survey burdens them, and driver stats are asked for separately by email.
processes.automation: Pull the driver counts from existing system reports instead of surveys, and send automatic reminders only to non-responders.

processes.name: Intercompany / interdesk reconciliation, allocation and invoice cleanup
processes.description: Logistics and allocation staff work lists of open meter, allocation and invoice issues (interconnect report, unfinaled invoices, Duke and CILCO deals). Each item is chased by email among schedulers, accounting and Daren, with deadlines set by management.
processes.stall_points: Items sit waiting on one person's decision, and the same question is forwarded many times. Accounting cannot redraft invoices until the allocation is fixed and bridged the next day.
processes.automation: A tracked issue list with owner, due date and automatic reminders, plus variance detection between desk-to-desk volumes. This would replace the manually updated email lists.

processes.name: New trading book and portfolio setup requests
processes.description: Darron Giron requests new books and portfolios across Tagg, Sitara and Global Counterparty, and curve-mapping or subregion changes. Each request goes to a different group and the status is chased by email.
processes.stall_points: The routing is unclear. A Tagg book must first be added in Global Counterparty, so the request is re-sent, and Darron cannot see whether a Sitara book exists until he asks.
processes.automation: One intake form that routes a new book to Global Counterparty, Tagg and Sitara together and shows its status. Book-to-pipe mappings could be reused from existing business units.

processes.name: Origination and transport invoice reconciliation on the Central desk
processes.description: Daily origination recognised by books is reconciled by the P&L analyst, who emails Darron with differences, and Darron checks which book granted it. Finance also asks him to update Sitara deals for finalized transport invoices.
processes.stall_points: Small unexplained dollar differences ($468) are carried across several emails. Darron has to look through books manually to find who granted the amount.
processes.automation: Auto-reconcile origination granted against recognised by book and flag only residual differences. Apply invoice amounts to Sitara deals from a feed.

processes.name: Monthly volumetric and fuel variance explanations and reports
processes.description: Business analysts ask commercial and logistics staff for explanations of volume variances, accrual breakdowns, fuel estimates and monthly reports. Replies are assembled by hand from separate reports and spreadsheets.
processes.stall_points: Requesters do not know the source of figures, for example 'What is the source of the numbers for the fuel'. Analysts must go back to logistics for each explanation, and deadlines are tight.
processes.automation: Generate the variance report and flag +/-10% changes automatically with drill-down. Pre-populate the transport tickets and accrual breakdowns.

processes.name: Mid-year PRC feedback and accomplishments collection
processes.description: Managers chase staff for performance feedback, accomplishment lists and headcount names ahead of PRC meetings. People respond by email, and reminders are sent when deadlines slip.
processes.stall_points: Feedback is requested repeatedly with deadlines before the system closes, and agenda clarifications are sent in long forwarded chains.
processes.automation: Automated reminders and a single collection form for accomplishments. Pre-fill names for the PRC list.
